title: TypeScript Type Narrowing Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on how TypeScript narrows types at runtime checks: typeof, instanceof, in, equality, discriminated unions, never exhaustiveness, type guards and assertion functions.

chapters.title: Narrowing Mental Model
points: Narrowing: TypeScript refines a union type to a more specific one inside a branch based on control-flow analysis of runtime checks
typeof x === 'string' narrows primitives; it returns 'string' | 'number' | 'bigint' | 'boolean' | 'symbol' | 'undefined' | 'object' | 'function'
Gotcha: typeof null === 'object', so typeof x === 'object' leaves null in the type until you check x !== null
Truthiness narrowing removes null/undefined but also removes 0, '' and NaN, so use x != null or x !== undefined when falsy values are valid

Narrowing resets after reassignment and does not survive into callbacks for a let variable that is reassigned after the callback is created (since TS 5.4, narrowing is kept in closures created after the last assignment)

chapters.title: Built-in Narrowing Operators
points: instanceof checks the prototype chain and narrows to a class type: if (e instanceof Error) { e.message }
instanceof does not work on interfaces or type aliases (they are erased) and fails across realms such as iframes
'key' in obj narrows a union to the members that have (or may have) that property: if ('swim' in pet) pet.swim()
Equality narrowing: === and !== between two typed values narrows both to the common type; x == null checks both null and undefined
Array.isArray(x) narrows a union to its array member (string[] for string | string[]; any[] for unknown) and is the standard way to split T | T[]

chapters.title: Discriminated Unions
points: A discriminated union has a shared literal-typed tag field: type Shape = { kind: 'circle'; r: number } | { kind: 'square'; side: number }
switch (s.kind) or if (s.kind === 'circle') narrows s to exactly one member in each branch
The tag must be a literal type (string, number, boolean, null or undefined literal), not plain string, or narrowing fails
Prefer a tagged union over optional fields such as { ok?: boolean; data?: T; error?: E } to make illegal states unrepresentable
Result pattern: type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: Error } narrows via if (r.ok)

chapters.title: Exhaustiveness with never
points: In the default branch of a fully handled switch, the remaining type is never
Helper: function assertNever(x: never): never { throw new Error('Unexpected: ' + x) } called in default
Adding a new union member makes the default branch's value non-never, so the assertNever call fails to compile and flags every unhandled switch
Alternative without a helper: const _exhaustive: never = s; in default
Gotcha: assertNever only protects at compile time, so untrusted runtime data (JSON, APIs) can still hit it and needs validation

chapters.title: Custom Guards and Assertion Functions
points: User-defined type guard: function isFish(p: Fish | Bird): p is Fish { return 'swim' in p } narrows in the true branch and excludes Fish in the false branch
A return type of boolean does not narrow, so the type predicate 'p is Fish' is required
TypeScript does not verify the predicate body, so a wrong guard (for example returning true for everything) silently produces unsound types
Assertion function: function assertIsString(v: unknown): asserts v is string { if (typeof v !== 'string') throw new Error() } narrows the rest of the scope after the call
asserts cond (no type) narrows by condition, e.g. asserts x != null; assertion functions must be called through an explicitly typed reference and must throw on failure

chapters.title: Narrowing Cheat Sheet
points: typeof: primitives and function; instanceof: class instances; in: property presence; === / == null: literals and null checks
Discriminated union: literal tag plus switch, with default: assertNever(x) for exhaustiveness
Guard 'x is T' returns boolean and narrows both branches; assertion 'asserts x is T' throws and narrows afterwards
Pick by data: unknown input uses typeof or a guard, object unions use a tag or in, class hierarchies use instanceof
Pitfalls: typeof null is 'object', truthiness drops 0 and '', interfaces cannot use instanceof, guard bodies are unchecked
